environment.description: Same application code deployed on EC2 (identical AMI, JDK, Tomcat, classpath). However, the EC2 instance resides in a private subnet with no internet-facing ingress. Traffic is routed exclusively through an AWS Lambda Function URL (https://abc123.lambda-url.us-east-1.on.aws/) configured with AuthType: AWS_IAM. The Lambda function acts as a thin proxy that forwards validated requests to the EC2 instance via VPC-internal ALB. The Lambda Function URL's resource-based policy specifies an explicit principal condition: {"Condition":{"StringEquals":{"lambda:FunctionUrlAuthType":"AWS_IAM"}},"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/WMSServiceRole"},"Action":"lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl"}. No wildcard principals. No public access. The Lambda itself performs request forwarding without content inspection - it passes the raw body through to the internal ALB target. CloudTrail logging is enabled but no active blocking based on payload content.
